drivingQuestion: How could Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi belch, yawn, sneeze and spit while praying if a baraita treats each of these as blameworthy?
outcomeNote: Each limb of the contradiction is resolved by a distinction, and Rabbi's conduct is left intact; Ravina's variant practice is defended by his fastidiousness.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי אֶת רַבִּי שֶׁגִּיהֵק וּפִיהֵק וְנִתְעַטֵּשׁ וְרָק
segments.en: Since Rabbi Ḥanina related a story involving Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, the Gemara cites another such story. «Rabbi Ḥanina said: I saw Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi, while he was praying, «belch, yawn, sneeze, spit,»

segments.he: וּמְמַשְׁמֵשׁ בְּבִגְדוֹ, אֲבָל לֹא הָיָה מִתְעַטֵּף. וּכְשֶׁהוּא מְפַהֵק הָיָה מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ עַל סַנְטֵרוֹ.
segments.en: «and» if he was stung by a louse, he may «feel» for it and remove it «with his garment, but he would not wrap himself» in his prayer shawl if it fell during prayer. «And when he would yawn he would place his hand on his chin» so that his open mouth would not be visible.

segments.he: מֵיתִיבִי: הַמַּשְׁמִיעַ קוֹלוֹ בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ — הֲרֵי זֶה מִקְּטַנֵּי אֲמָנָה. הַמַּגְבִּיהַּ קוֹלוֹ בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ הֲרֵי זֶה מִנְּבִיאֵי הַשֶּׁקֶר.
segments.en: The Gemara «raises an objection» based on a baraita: «One who sounds his voice during his» Amida «prayer is among those of little faith,» as he seems to believe that the Lord cannot hear his prayer when it is uttered silently. «One who raises his voice during prayer is» considered to be «among the false prophets,» as they too were wont to cry out and shout to their gods.

segments.he: מְגַהֵק וּמְפַהֵק — הֲרֵי זֶה מִגַּסֵּי הָרוּחַ. הַמִּתְעַטֵּשׁ בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ — סִימָן רַע לוֹ. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: נִיכָּר שֶׁהוּא מְכוֹעָר. הָרָק בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ — כְּאִילּוּ רָק בִּפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ.
segments.en: Furthermore, one who «belches and yawns» while praying «is surely among the uncouth. One who sneezes during his prayer, for him it is a bad omen. And some say: It is clear that he is repulsive.» Also, «one who spits during prayer, it is tantamount to spitting in the face of the king.» In light of all this, how could Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi have done all that while praying?

segments.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא מְגַהֵק וּמְפַהֵק לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן לְאוֹנְסוֹ, כָּאן לִרְצוֹנוֹ. אֶלָּא מִתְעַטֵּשׁ אַמִּתְעַטֵּשׁ קַשְׁיָא!
segments.en: The Gemara explains: «Granted,» with regard to «one who belches and yawns, it is not difficult: Here,» in the case where Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi did so, «it was involuntary» and therefore permissible; «here,» where it is considered uncouth, is in a case where «it is deliberate.» However, the contradiction «between sneezing» in the case where Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi did so «and sneezing» where it is considered a bad omen «is difficult.»

segments.he: מִתְעַטֵּשׁ אַמִּתְעַטֵּשׁ נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן מִלְּמַעְלָה, כָּאן מִלְּמַטָּה. דְּאָמַר רַב זֵירָא: הָא מִילְּתָא אִבַּלְעָא לִי בֵּי רַב הַמְנוּנָא וּתְקִילָא לִי כִּי כּוּלֵּי תַּלְמוּדַאי: הַמִּתְעַטֵּשׁ בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ סִימָן יָפֶה לוֹ, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁעוֹשִׂים לוֹ נַחַת רוּחַ מִלְּמַטָּה, כָּךְ עוֹשִׂים לוֹ נַחַת רוּחַ מִלְּמַעְלָה.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: The contradiction «between sneezing» in one case «and sneezing» in the other case «is also not difficult: Here,» in the case of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, it is referring to sneezing «from above,» his nose; «here,» where it is a bad omen, is referring to sneezing «from below,» flatulence. «As Rav Zeira said: In the school of Rav Hamnuna I absorbed this matter» in passing, «and it is equal» in significance «to all the rest of my learning: One who sneezes in the midst of prayer, it is a good omen for him. Just as» the sneeze soothes his irritation, «giving him pleasure below,» it is a sign that «they are similarly giving him pleasure above.» Since Rav Zeira sneezed often, he was extremely pleased to hear this.

segments.he: אֶלָּא רָק אַרָק קַשְׁיָא! רָק אַרָק נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא, אֶפְשָׁר כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה. דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִילָּה וְנִזְדַּמֵּן לוֹ רוֹק — מַבְלִיעוֹ בְּטַלִּיתוֹ. וְאִם טַלִּית נָאֶה הוּא — מַבְלִיעוֹ בַּאֲפַרְקְסוּתוֹ. רָבִינָא הֲוָה קָאֵי אֲחוֹרֵי רַב אָשֵׁי, נִזְדַּמֵּן לוֹ רוֹק, פַּתְקֵיהּ לַאֲחוֹרֵיהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה מַבְלִיעוֹ בַּאֲפַרְקְסוּתוֹ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא אֲנִינָא דַּעְתַּאי.
segments.en: «However,» The contradiction «between spitting» in the case where Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi did so «and spitting» where it is deemed tantamount to spitting in the face of the king «is difficult.» The Gemara replies: The contradiction «between spitting» in one case «and spitting» in the other case «is also not difficult,» as «it is possible» to resolve it «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rav Yehuda,» as «Rav Yehuda said: One who was standing in prayer, and saliva happened» to accumulate in «his» mouth, «he absorbs it in his garment. And if it was a fine garment» and he does not want it to become sullied, «he may cover it up in his head covering.» That way, one is permitted to spit. The Gemara relates: «Ravina was standing behind Rav Ashi» during prayer when «saliva happened» to accumulate in «his» mouth, «so he discharged it behind him.» Rav Ashi «said to him:» And «does the Master not hold» in accordance with «that» statement of «Rav Yehuda, who said» that «one absorbs it in his head covering? He said to him: I am delicate,» and the mere knowledge that there is spittle in my head covering disturbs my prayer.

moves.summary: R' Ḥanina reports, in a further story about Rabbi begun earlier, that he saw Rabbi belch, yawn, sneeze and spit while praying
moves.about: what Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi did while praying — belching, yawning, sneezing, spitting, feeling for a louse through his garment

moves.summary: the Gemara objects from a baraita that condemns sounding the voice, belching, yawning, sneezing and spitting in prayer
moves.about: the baraita condemns belching, yawning, sneezing and spitting in prayer, yet Rabbi is reported to have done all four

moves.summary: belching and yawning are reconciled — Rabbi's were involuntary, the baraita speaks of the deliberate
moves.about: belching and yawning are condemned only when deliberate, and Rabbi's were involuntary

moves.summary: the sneezing limb of the contradiction is left standing by that answer
moves.about: the sneezing of the baraita against the sneezing of Rabbi remains unreconciled by the voluntary/involuntary distinction

moves.summary: sneezing from above is permitted, the bad omen concerns wind from below
moves.about: sneezing from above is permitted while the bad omen concerns wind from below

moves.summary: Rav Zeira's teaching, absorbed in Rav Hamnuna's study house, that sneezing in prayer is a good omen
moves.about: Rav Zeira's teaching that sneezing during prayer is a good omen, adduced to ground the above/below distinction

moves.summary: the spitting limb of the contradiction is now pressed
moves.about: spitting in prayer is likened to spitting before the king, yet Rabbi spat

moves.summary: spitting is permitted in Rav Yehuda's manner, absorbed in the garment
moves.about: spitting is permitted in the manner Rav Yehuda prescribed — absorbing it in one's garment or head covering

moves.summary: Rav Yehuda's ruling is quoted in full: absorb it in the garment, or in the head covering if the garment is fine
moves.about: Rav Yehuda's ruling that one standing in prayer absorbs saliva in his garment, or in his head covering if the garment is fine
